ac_cloud-notes.first_test: Has 1 shell tester, executed: test-cloud-notes-identity.sh, 9 assertions over a ONE-SHOT VENDORED tree. It guards the two ways a 173-file package rename fails silently. TOO LITTLE: a file the sweep missed keeps the upstream package - a compile error where it is a code reference, but NOT in the manifest, where an un-renamed ContentProvider authority means INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER on the owner's phone the day he also has a real Markor installed, a failure that never happens in CI. TOO MUCH: the sweep also rewrites the Apache-2.0 attribution it is legally required to preserve. It also pins build.json against app/build.gradle (applicationId, versionCode, versionName, and that gradle_task names a flavor this tree actually declares - Markor has THREE, so a task naming none of them is the green-run-that-published-nothing shape). Every assertion was mutation-tested before it was trusted: each was broken on purpose and watched go red, including a control proving the guard does not match its own explanatory comments. THE GAP, NAMED: the vendored tree ships 20 JVM unit test source files under app/src/test/java (GsTextUtilsTest, GsFileUtilsTest, Csv2MdTableTest, the markdown highlighter pattern tests, ...) and NONE of them execute. build.json::tests.unit is disabled deliberately, not by oversight: ship-cloud-notes.yml runs the test-engine step FIRST, before actions/setup-java and setup-android, so that it costs seconds and needs no toolchain - pointing tests.unit.task at a gradle task from there would invoke ./gradlew with no JDK and no Android SDK. Enabling them means moving the unit phase below SDK setup, which every sibling ship workflow would then also want; the task to enable is testFlavorDefaultDebugUnitTest. And nothing here is a rendered screen or an installed APK: no instrumentation test, no JVM in the container that maintains this app, and the phone was unreachable on 2026-09-11, so a green run proves the source has the right shape and never that the editor opens a folder of the owner's markdown.

ac_cloud-sheets.first_test: FOUR SHELL TESTERS, ALL NETWORK-BOUND BY NATURE, because every claim this app makes is about a REMOTE object — a pinned Gerrit revision and a sha256-pinned upstream APK. test-configure-flags-exist.sh derives the flag that carries our applicationId from upstream itself and caught --with-android-package-name, which exists nowhere upstream and which autoconf would have warned about and ignored, shipping the megabuild as org.collabora.app. test-engine-artefacts-in-apk.sh range-fetches the pinned APK's central directory and checks every row of tests/engine-artefacts.json, including the load-bearing negative — no .a and no .h anywhere in 6,375 entries. test-no-engine-build-required.sh (2026-09-11) is the one that decides the money: it proves against upstream at the pin that the engine reaches the APK through a jniLibs source dir, that CMake copies it rather than compiling it, that our patch series touches zero native files, and that the COOL bundle target reads no built engine — so #240's ~$35 megabuild is not needed for #224. Its three self-tests break a claim, a comment-only match and the native-file rule on purpose and require each to go red. NOT COVERED, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE GAP: nothing compiles this app. build.host is still null, patches/0002 (the declared --with-prebuilt-engine mode that configure.ac:884 still demands) is not written, and tests/patches-apply.sh proves only that the series APPLIES — it is deliberately not a test-*.sh because it costs a 471 MB Gerrit fetch. No tester here has ever seen this app build, and the artefact on the release shelf is still Collabora's own. ADDED 2026-09-11: test-jni-abi-matches-prebuilt.sh, which is the assertion the whole prebuilt-engine decision rests on. #277 ships COLLABORA'S libandroidapp.so against OUR Java compiled from upstream.online.revision, and those are different commits — the pin is an ordinary branch-tip commit, not the 26.04.3.1-155 release tag. JNI binds by symbol name at first call, so any native method added, removed or renamed between them yields a signed, published, installable APK that dies with UnsatisfiedLinkError when the document opens, after a wholly green build. It range-reads the .so out of the pinned APK, parses .dynsym, and requires the native methods declared in the Java at the pin to match the exported Java_* symbols exactly in both directions. Today they do: 8 symbols, LOActivity 7 and COWebViewClient 1. It cannot see a class that declares a native and has no symbol at all, because Gerrit cannot enumerate a tree without a 471 MB clone; that limit is written in the file's header rather than left for someone to assume away.

ac_cloud-writer.first_test: Has 6 shell testers, executed. Two prove the routing and the absence of a credential; two prove the four configuration pages exist AND are backed by this app's own store, which is the assertion task 209 lacked; two prove the Material 3 design system is in place and has not been undone — the toolchain restated in build.gradle still matches build.json, no screen draws outside the theme, no hardcoded hex palette or raw-pixel padding has crept back, the price table's cells are still single-line (task 214), and every home-screen card description exists in Spanish (task 221). The gap that remains is that NONE of this is a rendered screen: there is no instrumentation test and no JVM in the container that maintains this app, so a green run proves the APK compiles and the source has the right shape, never that the screen looks right. Only a device screenshot does that.
